clue.text: Long Island seafront has iron fence for those who work there?

parts.note: LI is the standard abbreviation for Long Island
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a guard is a protective barrier, like a fence
the front of the word sea

explanation.surface: A fence with iron in it has been put along the beach front on Long Island, presumably for the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The sea's front letter goes at the very end of the answer, after the iron fence. 'There' points back to the seafront, which is where these people work.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeguards are the staff who patrol a beach and swimming area, so they are the people working on a seafront.

clue.text: Chance of bravery when losing power

indicators.note: losing something means it is dropped, so a letter standing for the following word is removed

parts.note: pluck is courage
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone's prospects of showing courage fade as they lose their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUCK without its P leaves LUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck and chance are synonyms: both name the fortune that decides outcomes without design.

clue.text: Weary following delay

definitions.note: a verb here: to grow tired

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: Someone is tired after being held up, a familiar travel complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or lose energy, which is what weary means as a verb.

clue.text: Loan oligarch settled with whisky, for example

indicators.note: settled suggests things being put in order or arranged, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A loan to a rich Russian magnate was paid off in whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is distilled from fermented grain, so it is one example of grain alcohol.

clue.text: Pays attention when the evening news is shown on a handheld console

parts.note: News at Ten is the long-running ITV evening bulletin, so the news's own label is AT TEN
the Nintendo DS is a handheld games console

explanation.surface: Someone only follows the news when they can watch it on a games device.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a British TV news programme; in a down clue 'on' puts AT TEN above DS.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to something is to pay attention to it, so attends is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Black Widow might make this a place for criminal activity?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a black widow is a dark spider
second meaning: the hidden part of the internet where illegal trade goes on

explanation.surface: Capitalised, Black Widow reads as the Marvel superhero or a femme fatale, a natural figure to link with crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals mislead: here it is just the venomous black spider.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark web is the encrypted, unindexed part of the internet known for drug and data markets.

clue.text: Bird watching, foolishly ignoring wing

indicators.note: doing something foolishly means doing it wildly and without order, so the remaining letters get jumbled
ignoring means leaving out, so the letters of the word after it are removed

parts.note: taken as written
these four letters are taken out one by one

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher behaves foolishly by paying no attention to a bird's wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird watching' looks like one phrase, but Bird is the definition. Remove W, I, N and G from WATCHING to leave ATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is a small songbird, as in stonechat or whinchat.

clue.text: Bungle joins Paddington's family for a bit of breakfast

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to bungle it
Paddington Bear lives with the Brown family

explanation.surface: Bungle, the bear from the children's show Rainbow, joins Paddington Bear's household for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bungle is the bear from the British children's TV show Rainbow, which makes the surface a bear party; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash browns are fried grated potato cakes served as part of a cooked breakfast.

clue.text: Last bit of pine inserted into the joist later

indicators.note: something inserted into a thing is placed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the stays as THE, and a joist is a rafter

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last bit of the word pine

explanation.surface: A carpenter fits the end of a pine piece into a joist afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereafter means after that time, a formal synonym for later.

clue.text: Recast arch-villainous dramatis personae

indicators.note: villainous means wicked and corrupt, so the preceding letters are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A play's cast list has been recast with an arch-villain in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recast' looks like the anagram signal, and 'arch-villainous' like one word; in fact 'Recast arch' is the fodder and 'villainous' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatis personae is Latin for the persons of the drama, the list of characters in a play.

clue.text: Angel will reportedly land surrounded by water

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so what counts is how the words are spoken

parts.note: Angel is the setter, so the setter will is I will, contracted to I'll

explanation.surface: The setter promises, through a spokesperson, to touch down on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pen name; Angel set this puzzle, so 'Angel will' is 'I will'.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land with water all around it.

clue.text: Cryptic haters? Agony for lovers!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read in crossword style: the word hearts broken up and reordered spells haters
second meaning: the grief of a failed romance

explanation.surface: A cryptic note on those who hate, followed by an outburst about the pain of love.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half describes the answer as a crossword device: broken is a rearranging signal and hearts is its fodder, which gives haters. 'Cryptic' flags that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken heart is the overwhelming sorrow after love is lost or rejected, so lovers suffer it.

clue.text: Following UN Article, rebel saw Assembly as impossible to argue against

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: assembly is putting parts together, so the preceding letters are built into a new order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rebel, citing a UN article, found the General Assembly's case watertight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly' with its capital looks like the UN General Assembly, but it is the signal to rearrange 'rebel saw'.
explanation.definitionFit: An unanswerable point is one nobody can refute, which is exactly what impossible to argue against means.

clue.text: Dreamed of cool siesta at sea on date

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused and adrift, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
d is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone imagined a nice cool nap on a boat on a particular day.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasise about something is to daydream about it, so fantasised matches dreamed of.

clue.text: Chalk-based treatment for skin complaint

definitions.note: the answer is plural while the definition is singular, read as the condition

indicators.note: a treatment processes or works on something, so the preceding letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A chalky remedy is offered for a skin problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackheads are small dark plugs in skin pores, a common form of acne and so a skin complaint.

clue.text: Basic building blocks found in Spain, Luxembourg and El Salvador, after all

indicators.note: after places the country letters behind the final word, which therefore comes first

parts.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain, from España
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
ES is the international vehicle code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: Fundamental components turn up in three countries after all, like a trade or science report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after all' sounds like a throwaway phrase, but it puts ALL at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleles are variant forms of a gene, the basic units of inheritance in genetics.

clue.text: Brownie unavailable, but required for this competition?

parts.note: a brownie is a bake, a baked item
a dish that is off is no longer on the menu

explanation.surface: The brownie is sold out, yet it is exactly what the baking contest demands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a hugely popular TV baking contest; 'Brownie' could also be a young Girl Guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A bake-off is a baking competition, the kind of event where a brownie would be entered.

clue.text: Confirm complete reprimand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mark an item on a list as done
second meaning: to scold someone, in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like an adjective on reprimand (a full telling-off), but it belongs with 'Confirm'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to check off a finished task and, informally in Britain, to scold.

clue.text: Sondheim's work in ruins?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1971 Stephen Sondheim musical
second meaning: ornamental buildings, often built as fake ruins on country estates

explanation.surface: Is a Sondheim show set among ruins, or is it a ruin itself?
explanation.walkthrough: A folly is a decorative structure on an English estate, often a sham ruined tower or temple.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical is called Follies, and garden follies were frequently built as deliberate ruins.

clue.text: Back flipper twirled cane

parts.note: a fin is a flipper

indicators.note: something twirled is spun round, so the following letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gymnast does a back flip while someone twirls a cane, a music-hall act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back flipper' reads as a gymnast, but Back is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a venture is to fund it, which is what finance means as a verb.

clue.text: Flimsy paper kept in folder

indicators.note: something kept in a holder sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a file is a folder for documents
a rag is a disparaging name for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Thin paper is stored in a folder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile describes something easily broken or delicate, a close synonym of flimsy.

clue.text: Recklessly serve alcohol for one who's just turned 18, perhaps

indicators.note: acting recklessly means acting wildly and carelessly, so the following letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A barman carelessly sells drink to someone barely of legal drinking age.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 18 is both the legal drinking age and the usual age for finishing school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school leaver is a pupil finishing secondary education, typically at about 18 in the UK.

clue.text: Call for quiet time

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a moment of silence.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to summon them, by loudspeaker or pager, so it means to call.

clue.text: In sex, empty seduction does not exist

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the following word

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex, as in sex appeal

indicators.note: an empty word has had its contents removed, so only its outside letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Hollow seduction means there is no real sex at all.
explanation.walkthrough: It meaning sex appeal is a crossword favourite from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something isn't, as in 'there isn't any', is to say it does not exist.

clue.text: Make a big noise when closing poetry event

definitions.text: Make a big noise when closing
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shut a door loudly
second meaning: a competitive live poetry performance

explanation.surface: A performer makes a loud finish to end a poetry reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Slamming a door shuts it with a bang, and a poetry slam is a performance contest for poets.

clue.text: Trips, and skirt splits

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
breaks is a synonym for splits

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and their skirt rips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips' reads as a verb for stumbling, but it is the plural noun for journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Minibreaks are short holidays, usually a weekend away, so they are trips.

clue.text: Table divides kitchen section

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut from something larger, so the letters are found inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A worktop splits a kitchen into areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitchen section' looks like a single phrase; section is the signal, and the answer straddles 'divides kitchen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk is a table used for writing or office work, so table serves as a near-synonym.

clue.text: Test fools men caught by virtuous woman

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: something caught by another is held within its grasp, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a virtuous person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trial in which foolish men are caught out by a virtuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation such as an exam, so it is a test.
